sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: In a trial of 1,137 adults with resected melanoma, the personalised mRNA vaccine intismeran combined with the immunotherapy drug pembrolizumab cut the risk of cancer returning or death by 42% after two years. Additionally, 82% of patients receiving the combined treatment remained alive and recurrence-free, compared with 70% taking immunotherapy alone.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: It is the first individualised cancer vaccine to show positive phase III trial results. The vaccine targets up to 34 unique genetic mutations from a patient's tumour to train the immune system to prevent cancer returning.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Results will be presented at a Madrid conference and published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Manufacturers MSD and Moderna are seeking regulatory approval and testing the vaccine against lung, bladder and kidney cancers.

gist: Retail sales in Great Britain fell 0.4% in September as households reduced spending.
Unseasonably warm weather affected autumn clothing sales, while fuel sales increased significantly.
Consumer confidence dropped rapidly ahead of the chancellor's upcoming budget announcement.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Retail sales volumes in Great Britain fell by 0.4% in September, driven by reduced online shopping and lower sales of autumn clothing due to warm weather. Household goods and supermarket sales also declined, whereas department store sales rose by 0.2% and motor fuel volume grew by 2.2%.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The drop in sales highlights growing financial pressure on households alongside a rapid decline in UK consumer confidence ahead of the festive period. It marks a negative update before Chancellor John Healey presents the budget.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Capital Economics forecasts that real consumer spending and real GDP growth will stall in the fourth quarter and early next year. The drop in confidence also reduces the likelihood of an early election.

articles.standfirst: Economic fallout from war in Middle East adds to pressures on consumers and on chancellor before budget

gist: UK consumer confidence fell by 11 percentage points in October.
The drop is the fastest rate outside the Covid pandemic since 2016.
Rising cost of living and Middle East conflict drive the decline.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: UK consumer confidence fell by 11 percentage points to -24 in October, marking the fastest monthly drop outside the Covid pandemic since the July 2016 Brexit vote. The GfK index recorded declines as inflation rose to 3.5% and households faced surging fuel, diesel and energy prices.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The squeeze on living standards comes ahead of the budget statement. The chancellor faces pressure to support households as borrowing costs reach the highest level in decades and the government deficit hits £24.5bn.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The chancellor has pledged to announce breathing space measures in his upcoming budget statement to ease pressure on households.
